annotations.title: Estimate a simulation's cost and size before running it

description: Predicts how large a run of a model will be and how many credits it will cost, without running it. Use this before running a large or unfamiliar model, or to check that an account can afford it. It does not look for mistakes; use check_simulation_model for that. It returns the number of trials, time periods, nodes and edges, the estimated peak memory in MB, a complexity score, the size tier (small or large), the credit cost for an account, and a rough run time in seconds for run_monte_carlo_simulation and for rank_inputs_by_impact (which runs the model many times). Runs over about 40 seconds (150 seconds without an account) continue in the background and are collected with get_simulation_results. A run is small when trials × nodes × time periods is at most 100,000, and large otherwise. Accounts have no fixed trial or node limit. That cost is what run_monte_carlo_simulation, summarize_outcome_scenarios and rank_inputs_by_impact each charge for this model. A model with mistakes returns an error instead of an estimate. Cost: free, with or without an account -- it debits no credits and spends none of your free daily runs. Without an account, a model over 1,000 trials or 20 nodes is rejected, also at no cost.

graph.description: The model: root_nodes (uncertain inputs), calc_nodes (formulas), edges (links; formulas refer to them like {e1}) and run_params (trials and time periods). Same format as run_monte_carlo_simulation's graph, which documents formulas, periods, distributions and financial metrics in full. Only this outline is published here: the full schema is on run_monte_carlo_simulation's graph parameter, and the neumann://catalog resource lists every distribution and formula function. Neumann checks the model against that full schema when you call this tool and names any problem.
